validated_results.title: An Unusual Case Report: Occurrence of Renal Cell Carcinoma, Basal Cell Carcinoma and Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia in a Case of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Treated with Radioactive Iodine.
validated_results.reason: The iodine exposure here is therapeutic radioactive iodine ablation after thyroidectomy, a medical treatment rather than a nutritional iodine exposure, reported in a single non-comparative case.

validated_results.title: The Association Between Ascorbate and the Hypoxia-Inducible Factors in Human Renal Cell Carcinoma Requires a Functional Von Hippel-Lindau Protein.
validated_results.reason: Ascorbate was measured in resected tumor tissue to correlate with HIF pathway activation and mechanism, providing no evidence on the risk of developing clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

validated_results.title: The Association Between Ascorbate and the Hypoxia-Inducible Factors in Human Renal Cell Carcinoma Requires a Functional Von Hippel-Lindau Protein.
validated_results.reason: Tumor-tissue ascorbate content was related to HIF pathway scores in existing papillary tumors, a molecular mechanism analysis without any incidence outcome.

validated_results.title: The Association Between Ascorbate and the Hypoxia-Inducible Factors in Human Renal Cell Carcinoma Requires a Functional Von Hippel-Lindau Protein.
validated_results.reason: The study compares tumor versus cortex ascorbate and HIF levels plus in vitro mechanisms, with no estimate of renal cell carcinoma incidence.

validated_results.title: Soy Isoflavones Protect Normal Tissues While Enhancing Radiation Responses.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of studies on soy isoflavone-radiation interaction in preclinical tumor models rather than an original human incidence study.

validated_results.title: The Effect of Daily Fluid Management and Beverages Consumption on the Risk of Bladder Cancer: A Meta-analysis of Observational Study.
validated_results.reason: The article is a meta-analysis of observational studies of fluid and beverage intake and bladder cancer risk, not primary data.

validated_results.title: The Effect of Daily Fluid Management and Beverages Consumption on the Risk of Bladder Cancer: A Meta-analysis of Observational Study.
validated_results.reason: The milk-bladder cancer estimate is a pooled summary relative risk from a meta-analysis of published observational studies.

validated_results.title: The Effect of Daily Fluid Management and Beverages Consumption on the Risk of Bladder Cancer: A Meta-analysis of Observational Study.
validated_results.reason: The tea-bladder cancer result derives from a dose-response meta-analysis of previously published studies rather than original human data.

validated_results.title: Low serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D is associated with increased bladder cancer risk: A systematic review and evidence of a potential mechanism.
validated_results.journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology
validated_results.reason: The human evidence is a systematic review of six published papers on serum 25(OH)D and bladder cancer risk, accompanied only by cell-line mechanistic experiments.

validated_results.title: Systematic review of modifiable risk factors for kidney cancer.
validated_results.reason: This is a systematic review summarizing published case-control and cohort studies of modifiable risk factors for kidney cancer.

cases.excerpt: This nested case-control analysis within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) investigated associations between pre-diagnostic serum folate, homocysteine, vitamins B6 and B12 and the risk of urothelial cell carcinomas of the bladder (UCC). A total of 824 patients with newly diagnosed UCC were matched with 824 cohort members.

effect_size.excerpt: A halving in serum folate concentrations was moderately associated with risk of UCC (OR: 1.18; 95% CI: 0.98-1.43), in particular aggressive UCC (OR: 1.34; 95% CI: 1.02-1.75; p-heterogeneity = 0.19).
